policy.name: Specialty Drug Policy RX-58: Dupilumab for severe asthma (synthetic)
policy.text: Dupilumab is medically necessary for severe asthma in patients 12 years or older when ALL of the following are met: (1) eosinophilic phenotype, shown by EITHER a blood eosinophil count of 150 cells/uL or greater within the past 12 months, OR a FeNO of 25 ppb or greater within the past 12 months; (2) at least 2 asthma exacerbations requiring systemic corticosteroids in the past 12 months, or at least 1 requiring hospitalization; (3) adherence to high-dose inhaled corticosteroid plus a second controller (LABA, LAMA or leukotriene antagonist) for at least 3 consecutive months before the request; (4) pre-bronchodilator FEV1 below 80% predicted within the past 12 months; (5) the patient is not a current smoker; (6) dupilumab will not be used in combination with another biologic for asthma; (7) prescribed by or in consultation with a pulmonologist or allergist.

documents.name: Pre-auth request form
documents.text: Requested: dupilumab 600 mg loading dose, then 300 mg subcutaneous every 2 weeks. Diagnosis: severe persistent asthma, uncomplicated (J45.50). Prescriber: Dr. R. Iyer, pulmonology. Prescriber signature date: [blank].

documents.name: Pulmonology consult
documents.text: 37-year-old man with severe persistent asthma since childhood. Former smoker, 5 pack-years, quit 2019. Current controllers: high-dose ICS/LABA fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 mcg one inhalation twice daily and montelukast 10 mg nightly, both since 2025-11. Omalizumab from 2025-12 to 2026-06, stopped for lack of response. Three oral corticosteroid courses for exacerbations in the past 12 months (December 2025, March 2026, August 2026). Exam: diffuse expiratory wheeze. Inhaler technique reviewed and adequate. Plan: start dupilumab.

documents.name: Lab results
documents.text: CBC 2026-02-11: absolute eosinophils 410 cells/uL. CBC 2026-08-19: absolute eosinophils 120 cells/uL (drawn on day 3 of prednisone 40 mg burst). Urine cotinine 2026-09-30: negative. FeNO: not performed.

documents.name: Pulmonary function test
documents.text: Spirometry: pre-bronchodilator FEV1 2.41 L (64% predicted); post-bronchodilator FEV1 2.78 L (74% predicted). FEV1/FVC 0.62. Significant bronchodilator response.

documents.name: Emergency department visit
documents.text: Triage: Tobacco use: current every day smoker. Chief complaint: shortness of breath and wheeze for 2 days. SpO2 91% on room air. Treated with methylprednisolone 125 mg IV and nebulized albuterol/ipratropium. Discharged home on prednisone 40 mg daily for 5 days.

documents.name: Pharmacy fill history
documents.text: Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 filled 2026-05-02, 2026-06-01, 2026-07-03, 2026-08-01, 2026-09-02, 2026-10-01. Montelukast 10 mg filled on the same dates. Prednisone 20 mg tablets filled 2025-12-09 and 2026-08-17.

documents.name: PCP note
documents.text: Asthma flare after viral upper respiratory infection. Given prednisone 40 mg daily for 5 days from clinic sample stock. Follow up with pulmonology.

documents.name: UR nurse pre-review
documents.text: Most recent eosinophil count 120, below the 150 threshold. Patient listed as current smoker on ED record. Prior biologic (omalizumab) on file. Recommend physician review for denial.
